clue.text: Train fish to go back, changing its direction

indicators.note: going back tells us to read the fish's name from right to left

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the little word its are rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An instruction to train a fish to turn round and swim the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns CARP into PRAC; 'changing' rearranges ITS into TIS; E for east ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to rehearse or drill repeatedly; British spelling uses -ise for the verb.

parts.note: read stuck-up as pasted on a wall, a bill; and a clerk who posts entries in a ledger is one who posts

explanation.surface: A snooty office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck-up' looks like snobbish, but it means literally pasted up on a wall; a clerk who enters items in a ledger 'posts' them.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard pasted up in public is a bill, and someone who posts ledger entries fits the same word.

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the two words stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity is given a test run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges A TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila, the eagle.

clue.text: Will try to get the Manet reproduction

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: a reproduction of a painting is a copy, here the painter's name with its letters remade

explanation.surface: A will tries to get hold of a copy of a Manet painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduction' rearranges MANET into AMENT; 'to get the' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is the legal document disposing of a person's estate after death.

indicators.note: a fabrication is something made up, so the letters are constructed anew

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone from Dickens can deny that a story was made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabrication' rearranges CAN DENY STORY; the possessive 's adds no letter. Sydney Carton is the hero of A Tale of Two Cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney Carton is a character created by Charles Dickens, in A Tale of Two Cities.

clue.text: Be stingy, having a thousand in share certificates

indicators.note: in places the thousand inside the certificates

parts.note: scrip is a certificate entitling the holder to shares
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone is mean despite owning a thousand share certificates.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stingy is to economise meanly, skimping on spending.

clue.text: US Intelligence ? No, a Fascist chief

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is this American intelligence? No, it is a Fascist leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Galeazzo Ciano was Mussolini's son-in-law and Italian foreign minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Ciano was a leading figure in Mussolini's Fascist government, its foreign minister.

clue.text: Copied — otherwise made it in duplicate

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in a different arrangement
in duplicate means the little word appears twice

explanation.surface: It was copied; or else someone made two copies of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in duplicate' doubles IT to ITIT; 'otherwise' rearranges MADE with ITIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to mimic or reproduce what they do.

definitions.meaning: the takings from a sale or event

explanation.surface: Someone carries on making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' and 'perhaps' are links; the noun sense is takings, as in the proceeds of a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Goes forward is one sense of the verb; the noun means income raised by a sale or event.

definitions.meaning: at the Wimbledon tennis championships, one set to each side would leave the match level

explanation.surface: A reserve player, level in the tennis at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; read the answer as 'set a side', a set won by each side, so the score is even.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for future use is to earmark it; a set apiece makes a tennis match level.

clue.text: Cloth bill returned to firm, about £1

indicators.note: returned means the bill's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
L is the pound sign's letter and I is one
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Cloth whose bill was sent back to the firm, costing about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the bill backwards; 'about' sits loosely as a link, with the pound sign giving L and the 1 giving I before the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton fabric.

clue.text: Iris confounded tutor with this catch

parts.note: Iris was the Greek goddess of the rainbow

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters of the teacher are muddled

explanation.surface: A girl named Iris baffled her tutor with a fish she caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' rearranges TUTOR into TROUT; Iris personified the rainbow in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow trout is a game fish anglers catch.

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A woman is slightly hysterical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes a run of letters from inside 'hysterical'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Lay down flags, on retreat, so to speak, and vanish

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the paving word is read right to left

parts.note: to pave is to lay flagstones
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Soldiers lay down their flags in retreat, speak, and disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' are flagstones, not banners; 'on retreat' turns PAVE into EVAP, and 'so to' links to 'speak'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that evaporates disappears into vapour, so to vanish.

parts.note: beacons are signal lights
a field is a piece of ground

explanation.surface: Lights shining on some land in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire is a county north-west of London; the definition is a town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaconsfield is a market town in that county, from which Disraeli took his earldom.

clue.text: Whereby a composer gave his country a first-class turn-up

parts.note: the composer Sibelius was a Finn, so his country is Finland

indicators.note: a turn-up in a down entry means the letters are flipped upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A composer gave his nation a first-rate surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' turns AI into IA; 'a' is a link. Sibelius's tone poem Finlandia became a Finnish national anthem in all but name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibelius's patriotic tone poem was his gift to the Finnish people in their struggle for identity.

annotationWithheld.why: Hurries temporary resident aboard ? (8): CAMPER inside SS, but 'aboard' must give both SS (on a ship) and the container signal, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Report is given round in the end

parts.note: a round of ammunition is a bullet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A report is given out in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is ammunition, not a circle; 'is given' and 'the end' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement.

parts.note: to parry a blow is to counter it
a point is a score in a game

explanation.surface: A score by Parry, the English composer, would be well known to other composers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hubert Parry is the composer of Jerusalem, but here 'parry' is a fencer's block and 'score' a point won.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterpoint is the art of combining melodic lines, a technique every composer studies.

definitions.meaning: the coiled ... that drives a mechanical watch
the season of the year after winter

explanation.surface: A piece of a watch belongs to the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled mainspring powers a clockwork watch, and the season between winter and summer shares the name.

parts.note: de is the French for of
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: A modest supply of foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' asks for 'of' in French, DE; 'supply' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent in the sense of seemly, proper and not showy.

clue.text: Clumsy translation of Omar — it is about youth

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the youth
a translation renders words afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A clumsy version of Omar Khayyam's poem concerns a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges the poet's name with 'it', and 'about' wraps that round the youth: MA(LAD)ROIT. 'Omar' recalls Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat, famous in translation; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means lacking skill, awkward with one's hands or in manner.

definitions.meaning: the dentist's tool is bad news for the patient

explanation.surface: A dentist's tedious bad news for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as DR ILL: a doctor who is unwell is bad news for the patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill is to bore a hole, and a dentist's drill is what a patient dreads.

clue.text: Liberal is perhaps bitter about member

indicators.note: about places the beer around the member

parts.note: bitter is a kind of ale, so perhaps marks an example
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is perhaps bitter about a member.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is an English style of beer, here a kind of ALE; 'is' links. 'Liberal' looks like the party, but it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of plentiful or generous.

clue.text: Necessitate a one pound ten outlay

indicators.note: an outlay spends things out differently, read as laying the letters out anew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An expense of one pound ten shillings is unavoidable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlay' rearranges A, I, L and TEN; a pound ten was an old price, one pound ten shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require it as a consequence.

definitions.meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Titania's bower is over-canopied with this plant

explanation.surface: The honeysuckle that sheltered the fairy queen as she slept.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, sleeping 'quite over-canopied with luscious' honeysuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodbine is a common name for wild honeysuckle, named in Oberon's speech about Titania's bed.

indicators.note: unfinished means the garment's final letter is left off

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest

explanation.surface: A single garment left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' removes the last letter, T, from SINGLET, a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one only, solitary.

parts.note: an honest deal is a fair one, and in poker a run of five cards in sequence also takes this name

explanation.surface: A fair bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Honest means upright, and a 'deal' in poker can produce a five-card sequence of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest and frank, and a straight is a poker hand dealt in sequence.
